title: REAR BRAKE LINES
summary: Rear brake lines: the rear-circuit pipe runs from the master cylinder back along the LH frame rail in screwed-down clips to the LH rear hose connector; a crossover pipe runs across the rear of the frame to the RH connector. At each side a flexible rear brake hose is held in the frame bracket by a spring clip and feeds a pipe along the trailing arm to the rear caliper.

fastening.to: master cylinder rear outlet and LH rear connector [5]
fastening.note: Pipe [10] tube nuts (torque 1); pipe runs back along the LH frame rail and turns up to the hose connection at the kickup.
Clips [9] each held by a screw [3] (callouts '9 3 torque 2' at 4 places along the rail plus one at the front by the master cylinder); a further clip [9] on the vertical run at the kickup.
Clip [2] with screw [3] holds the crossover pipe [1] at the frame.
Clip [4] holds the pipe on the frame near the LH connector; no screw shown with it.
View A: hose [8] threads into the connector [11] (torque 4) through the frame bracket; spring [6] slides over the hose fitting to lock it in the bracket. Same at LH connector [5].
Pipe [7] runs along the trailing arm from the hose to the caliper (torque 3).

notes: Maximum allowable twist during asm. of rear brake hoses is ± one notch at bracket.

With wheels straight ahead and suspension in full rebound, insert the hose into the frame bracket without kinking or twisting and install the retainer spring as shown; the paint stripe on the hose shows any kink or twist.
